novelty.justification: The novelty route is a new mechanistic relationship: the claim predicts that a protein model contains a “mechanism subspace that partially transcends homology,” such that “convergent same-mechanism enzymes will cluster” while homologous enzymes with divergent mechanisms separate. Searches using “protein language model catalytic mechanism M-CSA,” “enzyme embeddings convergent evolution homology,” “protein language model EC representation catalytic residues,” and “mechanism versus homology enzyme embeddings” identify Rives et al. (2021), ECPICK (2023), ProteinClusterTools (2025), and EC-Bench (2025) as the closest work, but these establish function/EC decoding, motif attribution, or embedding-based isofunctional clustering rather than explicitly representing shared reaction chemistry across convergent enzymes. Moving from those studies to a controlled convergence-versus-divergence account is a substantive multi-step integration and new unit of analysis, but remains a natural extension of established EC probing and homology-controlled function prediction rather than a wholly new interpretability paradigm.
